v1.curve.advancedPolyline.summary: Creates an advanced polyline definition using an array of point-line definitions. A polyline must start with an initial point-line definition (pld) using absolute coordinates: `{ xa: value, ya: value }` Subsequent points can be defined in multiple ways: - **Absolute coordinates**: `{ xa: value, ya: value }` - **Relative coordinates**: `{ xr: value, yr: value }` - **Mixed mode**: `{ xa: value, yr: value }` or `{ xr: value, ya: value }` A segment can also be defined using angle and length: - **Absolute angle and length**: `{ l: value, a: angle }` - The angle is measured counterclockwise (CCW) from the x-axis. - **Relative angle and length**: `{ l: value, ar: angle }` - The angle is measured CCW from the previous segments direction. A segment can also be defined using angle and an absolute or relative coordinates. Angle is defined as above and length is calculated internally: - Examples of this: `{ xa: value, a: value }`, `{ xr: value, a: value }`, `{ yr: value, a: value }`, `{ ya: value, ar: value }` Each point-line definition can optionally have a radius `{ r: value }`, which creates an arc that is tangent to both the previous and next segments. When a radius is specified: - The defined point remains collinear with both adjacent segments but does not belong to the actual polyline. - Cannot be applied with chamfer on the same point. Each point-line definition can optionally have a chamfer `{ c: value }`, which creates a symmetric Chamfer of length `{ c: value }` also called edge distance, measured along the edge of the original part before the chamfer was applied. - Cannot be applied with fillet on the same point. The polyline can be closed (`close: true`), which connects the last point back to the first point. - If closed, the first point can also have a radius, forming a smooth transition.

The bulge is tan(a/4), a is the included angle for the arc between the two points. A bulge is positive for arcs directed counterclockwise when looking in opposite direction of the normal. A semicircle has the bulge 1, a straight line the bulge 0.

v1.sketch.setReferences.summary: Creates and sets the plane, axis and origin reference of the sketch

v1.sketch.sketchRegion.summary: Creates a sketch region for a given sketch from sketch geometry

v1.sketch.splitAllCurves.summary: Splits all curves in the given sketch at their mutual intersection points. Used together with trimCurves and splitCurvesMergeBack.

v1.sketch.splitCurve.summary: Splits curves at specified parameterized positions. Note: This requires exact normalized parameter values [0,1] for where to cut. These values correspond to the internal curve parameterization and are typically computed by the sketcher plugin (e.g., from intersection calculations). For most use cases where you want to split at intersections, prefer the preTrim/trim/postTrim workflow which computes split positions automatically.

v1.sketch.splitCurves.summary: Splits curves in specified parameterized positions

v1.sketch.trim.summary: Removes curve segments produced by preTrim. This is the second step of the trim workflow: preTrim ? trim ? postTrim. Pass the curve segment ids from the preTrim result to select which segments to remove.

v1.sketch.trimCurves.summary: Trims away curves, if they are suitable for trimming

v1.sketch.undoFillet.summary: Deletes an existing fillet by removing the arc and its constraints and connect lines again

v1.sketch.unlinkReferenceGeometry.summary: Unlinks "Use"-Geometry in sketch - sketch geometry still exists, but it is not connected to reference anymore

v1.sketch.updateDimension.summary: Updates the dimension of sketch geometry and recalculates the sketch

v1.sketch.updateDimensionPosition.summary: Updates the position of the dimension text

v1.sketch.updateSketchRegion.summary: Updates sketch regions with new sketch geometry

v1.solid.copy.summary: Creates a copy of the given solid

v1.solid.deleteSolid.summary: Deletes the given solids or all solids if no solids are provided.

v1.solid.extrusion.summary: Creates an extrusion by extruding a shape or sketch geometry

v1.solid.fillet.summary: Creates a fillet at the given edges. Edges can be of different solids.

v1.solid.merge.summary: Creates an merge between solids. This is NOT a union!

v1.solid.mirror.summary: Mirrors the given solid at defined plane

v1.solid.offset.summary: Creates an offset solid of the given solid Note: This functionality is a quite difficult and fragile one. Make sure you call it only on solids, where you can offset all faces, calculate the new trims AND dont change the topology of the solid i.e. the number of faces and edges remain the same.

v1.solid.revolve.summary: Creates a revolve by revolving a polyline

v1.solid.rotation.summary: Rotates the given solid by the given rotation vector. The vector is in coordinates of the part where the provided solid belongs to. First the z-part of the rotation vector is performed, then the y-part and finally the x-part.

v1.solid.scale.summary: Scales the given solid with a factor. The scale is in coordinates of the part where the provided solid belongs to.

v1.solid.section.summary: The given solid is sectioned at the given plane.

v1.solid.slice.summary: Cuts the given solid at defined plane. The part on the negative side of normal vector is removed

v1.solid.translation.summary: Translates the given solid by the given vector. The vector is in coordinates of the part where the provided solid belongs to.

v1.solid.useSolid.summary: This method allows you to work with solids from other features. The solids from the provided feature will be returned and available to use within the given entity injection feature.
